chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, is the Fitrah (alms of fasting) obligatory on the people of the villages (rural areas)?' He said, 'The Fitrah is obligatory on everyone who consumes sustenance, and upon him to pay from that sustance.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْبَوَادِي: The people of the villages or rural areas
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: The alms of fasting, a mandatory charity given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to pay Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Ishtibār, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Zakat al-Fitr is not restricted by geography but is tied to the consumption of sustenance, thereby including rural populations ('Ahl al-Bawadi'). This establishes the principle that the obligation is universal for those who partake in food, reflecting the social welfare intent of the charity to ensure all Muslims can celebrate Eid. The hadith underscores the egalitarian nature of Fitrana, linking it directly to basic nourishment rather than urban status.
